templates.text: Maternal cortisol surge tightens uterine vasculature, delaying fetal oxygen delivery.
Catecholamine spike redirects placental flow, starving fetal periphery.
Sympathetic flood constricts spiral arteries, dropping fetal heart rate variability.
Fetal HPA axis activates prematurely, flooding circulation with stress hormones.
Uterine muscle tension compresses intervillous spaces, reducing gas exchange.
Maternal hyperventilation shifts acid-base balance, stressing fetal chemoreceptors.
Adrenal medulla release narrows placental capillaries, forcing fetal bradycardia.
Fetal blood pressure rises as maternal fight-flight diverts oxygen away.
Glucocorticoid cascade inhibits fetal growth signals, prioritizing survival over development.
Umbilical artery resistance spikes, lowering fetal oxygen saturation by {percent}%.
Maternal norepinephrine shunts blood from uterus, triggering fetal hypoxic gasps.
Fetal heart rate accelerations vanish as sympathetic tone overrides vagal brake.
Placental perfusion drops sharply, drowning fetal tissues in metabolic waste.
Cortisol crosses the placenta, reprogramming fetal amygdala toward heightened alertness.
Maternal stress hormones suppress fetal insulin production, starving neurons of glucose.
Vasoconstriction of uterine arteries stalls fetal growth trajectory within minutes.
Fetal adrenal glands enlarge acutely, pumping out dehydroepiandrosterone into circulation.
Uteroplacental resistance doubles, forcing fetal left ventricle to labor against high afterload.
Maternal cortisol levels peak, disrupting fetal sleep-wake cycling and autonomic stability.
Fetal oxygenation index falls below threshold, activating primitive laryngeal chemoreflexes.
Beta-adrenergic activation relaxes fetal gut, increasing aspiration risk for meconium.
Placental 11β-HSD2 enzyme is overwhelmed, exposing fetal brain to maternal cortisol excess.
Fetal heart rate decelerates into shallow U-shapes as oxygen debt accumulates.
Maternal vasopressin release constricts spiral arterioles, starving placental villi of blood.
Fetal sympathetic chain fires continuously, depleting catecholamine reserves before delivery.
Transplacental oxygen gradient inverts, making fetal extraction of O₂ increasingly difficult.
Amniotic adrenaline rises, coating fetal lungs and blunting surfactant production.
Fetal baroreceptors reset upward, setting baseline blood pressure to a new high.
Maternal inflammatory cascade floods the placenta, stiffening vessel walls and narrowing flow.
Fetal cerebral autoregulation fails as mean arterial pressure swings beyond normal range.
